title: serve: let a plugin supply the ICryptoProvider for secret fields; today serve installs LocalCryptoProvider after every plugin hook, so a KMS-backed provider (cloud#3573) cannot be mounted
body:
repo:cloud#1 · os-baozhoutao · session_013w7BrxKc6dUYe6Rw6tQW4G

Filing gate: **④ coordination**, the platform half of objectstack-ai/cloud#3573 (p1). That card carries **③ a task on the maintainer's word**: 「同意立卡」, then 「相关任务都可以是 p1」 (2026-11-06).

**Business reason.** Enterprise security questionnaires ask for customer-managed keys. cloud#3573 has built KMS-backed `ICryptoProvider` implementations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Vault transit), branch `claude/issue-3573-kms-crypto-providers` on cloud. But no self-hosted `objectos-ee` boot can mount them, because `objectstack serve` decides the provider itself, after every plugin hook.

**Reader who acts.** The lane that owns `packages/cli` (triage sets lane and grade; cloud suggests p1, inherited from cloud#3573). Then the cloud seat wires the provider from a licence-gated `security-enterprise` plugin.

**Dedupe** (open and closed): `setCryptoProvider` and `crypto provider seam` searched on objectstack issues; no open card asks for a host-supplied provider.

## Measured (objectstack `main` `26c965cb`; the same block is at cloud's pin `c50e0dfa`)

`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, the "Secret-field CryptoProvider wiring (host composition root)" block, runs after `await runtime.start()`, i.e. after `kernel:ready` / `kernel:bootstrapped` / `kernel:listening`.
- When no `sharedCryptoProvider` exists, it builds a `LocalCryptoProvider`.
- It then always calls `dataEngine.setCryptoProvider(sharedCryptoProvider)`.
- The datasource binder shares the same instance.

So whatever a plugin set during init is overwritten. The block's own comment promises the seam that does not exist: "production hosts swap this for a KMS/Vault-backed provider (e.g. via an env-gated branch or a dedicated plugin) before secrets are written."

## Ask

`serve` consults a provider a plugin registered during init, under a kernel service name such as `crypto-provider`. It uses it for the data engine, the datasource binder and the default `SettingsServicePlugin`, and falls back to `LocalCryptoProvider` only when none is registered.
- Runtime wiring only: no spec key and no stack-config knob, so there is nothing for an AI author to write.
- The production refusal for an unstable local key stays as it is when the fallback is used.

## Done when

- A test plugin registering a provider during init sees secret-field writes sealed by it, and the binder uses the same instance.
- Without a registration, behaviour is byte-identical to today.
- cloud#3573 can then mount its provider from a plugin.
